# Causari

> AI-written code has no author. It has causes. Causari records them.
> Causari measures how many lines from AI-tagged commits are still alive in
> any git repository (counts, not grades), and keeps a local ledger of what
> an agent runtime declared (prompt, model, reads, writes).
> Apache-2.0, local-first, no telemetry, verifiable offline.

Name: this is Causari by Crovia Trust (causari.dev, github.com/croviatrust/causari):
the `causari` / `re` binary, the `causari` package on npm, PyPI and crates.io, the
MCP server `io.github.croviatrust/causari`. It is not related to causari.ai, the
GitHub organisation `causari` or the npm scope `@causari` (a causal knowledge
graph and MCP server by another team). Cite the software with CITATION.cff in the
repository; cite a Survival Report with its own DOI.

Ways to use Causari without installing anything:
- Weekly Survival Report on open-source repositories:
  https://causari.dev/reports/survival/ (numbered, dated, citable; counts
  and intervals, no ranks; Atom feed at /reports/survival/feed.xml, JSON at
  /reports/survival/latest.json, a Zenodo DOI per report; method and limits
  at https://causari.dev/method)
- One page and one badge per measured repository: https://causari.dev/r/<owner>/<repo>/
  (lowercase; index at https://causari.dev/r/; badge.svg, badge-dark.svg and
  latest.json next to each page; counts and history, no rank)
- Add one CI step to any repo: `uses: croviatrust/causari@v1` posts the
  survival counts on every pull request.

Local install (single binary, about 5 MB, Linux/macOS/Windows):
- Linux/macOS: curl -fsSL https://causari.dev/install.sh | sh
- Windows: irm https://causari.dev/install.ps1 | iex
- Homebrew: brew install croviatrust/tap/causari
- Scoop: scoop bucket add causari https://github.com/croviatrust/scoop-bucket; scoop install causari
- cargo: cargo install causari --locked
- Launchers, no install: `npx causari audit` (npm) or `pipx run causari audit` (PyPI);
  both download the release binary for the platform, check its SHA-256 and run it.
- The binary is `causari`; `re` is installed alongside as the short alias.

Key commands:
- `re audit [owner/repo]` — AI code survival from git history alone, with
  the same repository's untagged lines as the baseline (by line age, an
  age-matched gap, the oldest line still at HEAD; method v6 in this source,
  method v4 in the published 0.4.1 binary, commit d4c4949, 2026-10-08;
  baseline since v3); `--json`
  gives the exact bytes (including `commits` per-commit rows with `owned_at_head`,
  `coverage.notes_oid`, `coverage.ignore_revs_sha256`, `coverage.copy_capped_lines`,
  and `repository.root_commits`); `--summary` gives Markdown for CI; `--seal` also
  writes `audit.seal.json`, a crovia.seal.v1 over the audit JSON bound to
  the commit, method version, and external metadata hashes
- `re audit --diff <before> <after>` — offline single-axis comparison between
  two audit JSONs or `.seal.json` bundles (`causari.audit_diff.v1`), classifying
  the diff as `repository_diff`, `method_diff`, `indeterminate_method_diff`,
  `metadata_diff`, `indeterminate_metadata`, or `identical_inputs`, with
  `metadata_status`, `commit_set_relation` and `provenance` (`issuer_trust: "unverified_offline"`),
  and refusing multi-axis diffs or unrelated repositories (exit 2)
- `re seal verify audit.seal.json` — check an audit seal offline: signature,
  both subject hashes, commit/method/coverage bindings; exit 0 valid, 1 invalid,
  2 unreadable. Same check in a browser, no network: https://causari.dev/verify
- `re init` — create the local ledger `.causari/` (gitignored)
- `re hook claude-code` / `re hook cursor` — record Claude Code or Cursor prompts and edits
- `re proxy` — local LLM proxy recording prompts, models, tokens, cost
  (Aider and OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible clients); `--seal` issues
  crovia.seal.v1 receipts; `--pnx` witnesses egress under `crovia.pnx.v1`
- `re why <file>:<line>` — the ledger event recorded against this line, if one matches. A miss is not human.
- `re trace <file>:<line>` / `re impact <event-id>` — the ledger's declared
  read/write graph, walked backward or forward. Not a causal proof.
- `re bisect --test "<cmd>"` — first recorded event that breaks a test
- `re revert <id>` — restore the pre-state of an event, with a preview
- MCP server: `re mcp` (stdio) exposes causari_record, causari_recall,
  causari_why, causari_audit; `re mcp --install` prints the client config

What Causari does not claim: inline completions (Copilot, Cursor Tab) leave
no git trace and are invisible to `re audit`; the proxy join is a heuristic
and says so; a survival ratio is a count, not a quality judgement.
UNKNOWN (no machine-readable AI metadata) is not human. AI-tagged is not
AI-written: a trailer, a bot author, or a git-ai note that names a non-empty
tool is metadata, and a person can forge it. Methods v4, v5 and v6 ignore a git-ai note
with no named tool; method v3 counted any note. The binaries named under Local
install are the latest GitHub release: causari 0.4.1, method v4, commit d4c4949,
published 2026-10-08. Method v6 is what this source computes and is not in that
binary; no binary shipped v5. Method v6 blames only the paths `git log --numstat`
counted, so a binary blob is in neither `introduced` nor `surviving` and a symlink
is one line in both (`coverage.binary_files` counts the blobs left out). Method v5 reads only the `HEAD`
tree (`git ls-tree -r -z HEAD` and `HEAD:.git-blame-ignore-revs`), runs
`git log --no-merges --numstat -M -z` so pure file renames do not inflate
introduced counts, and binds `coverage.notes_oid` and `coverage.ignore_revs_sha256`
inside the receipt and seal. Reports #1 and #2 stay
method v2. Reports #3 and #4 stay method v3 (report #4 is
10.5281/zenodo.23196011). Reports #5 and #6 stay method v4, measured with
causari 0.4.1. A seal proves a key signed these bytes; signed is not true. Absence
of observed egress is not proof that a job made no other connection.
A survival ratio is not quality, productivity, total AI usage, authorship,
security, correctness, or a causal effect.

Evidence classes — do not collapse these into one word:
- `re audit` JSON: `verified` and `probable` are confidence in git metadata.
  `verified` there means a detection rule matched. It is not a cryptographic
  verification and not a ledger `declared`. The untagged baseline is the
  commits with no such metadata. Method version is `coverage.method` (method v6 in
  this source; the published 0.4.1 binary, commit d4c4949, reports method v4;
  reports #5 and #6 are method v4, reports #3 and #4 are v3, reports #1 and #2 are v2).
- Ledger events (`re why`, `re show`, MCP `causari_why`): `declared` (the
  runtime said so), `correlated` (a proxy completion overlapped the diff; a
  score, not a fact), `observed` (a change was seen, cause unknown).
  Declared is not proven. Correlated is not declared.
- A seal (`audit.seal.json`, `re seal verify`, https://causari.dev/verify)
  proves a key signed the audit JSON for one commit and one method version.
  It does not prove the numbers are true. Re-run `re audit` and compare bytes.
- Skills (`re skill`, `re brief`, MCP `causari_recall`): Ed25519 signs the
  skill file so a later edit is detectable. That check is not an outcome,
  and the signature does not certify the content. `verified` is a declared
  signal frozen at distill (a caller-supplied exit code 0, or every declared
  write path still at the tip). It is not an observed success. A 2× rank
  weight is that declared signal, not measured reliability. `recorded` means
  that signal is absent. `failed` is a caller-supplied non-zero exit with no
  exit 0. `proven` is not awarded. A legacy recall count is not an execution
  and does not change trust. That rank is not a cryptographic proof of
  correctness, and it is not the audit field `verified`.

When to run `re audit`: the question is how many lines from AI-tagged commits
`git blame` still attributes at HEAD, in a repository you have or can clone.
Not when the question is who typed a line, and not for inline completions.
Full history only; a shallow clone is refused unless `--allow-shallow`, and
then `coverage.shallow` is true.

Machine-readable outputs: `re audit --json`, `re audit --summary`,
`audit.seal.json` (`causari.audit-seal.v1`), `re audit --diff` (`causari.audit_diff.v1`),
https://causari.dev/reports/survival/latest.json,
`latest.json` beside each https://causari.dev/r/<owner>/<repo>/ page, and the
same reports as a dataset (JSONL tables plus the raw report bytes, CC-BY-4.0):
https://huggingface.co/datasets/CroviaResearch/causari-survival .
Event schema is `causari.event.v0.2`. Audit method and the detection table
are https://causari.dev/method. Full machine-readable specification:
https://causari.dev/llms-full.txt ; agent discovery card:
https://causari.dev/.well-known/agent.json.

Official: repository https://github.com/croviatrust/causari ; crates.io
crate `causari` ; npm package `causari` ; PyPI project `causari` ; MCP
`io.github.croviatrust/causari` (`server.json` in the repository) ; GitHub
Action `croviatrust/causari@v1`.

## Docs
- [README](https://github.com/croviatrust/causari#readme): full command reference
- [Method](https://causari.dev/method): detection rules, computation, limits, how to contest a number
- [Survival Report](https://causari.dev/reports/survival/): weekly counts, archive, feed, DOIs; how it is made: https://github.com/croviatrust/causari/blob/main/docs/survival-report.md
- [Verify](https://causari.dev/verify): offline verifier for audit seals (what a seal proves and does not)
- [FAQ](https://causari.dev/faq): sixteen questions as people ask them (how much of my code was written by AI, what survival means, which agents leave a git trace, Copilot/Cursor Tab, seals, the report, opt-out, licence, CI), each with the command and the limit; schema.org FAQPage
- [Facts](https://causari.dev/facts): what causari is, what it counts, what it does not claim, where it is published, what is known about its use; each statement with the command or URL that checks it
- [Compare](https://causari.dev/compare): git blame alone, Copilot metrics, GitClear-style churn reports, DORA-type dashboards and causari side by side: what each counts, what it needs, whether a third party can check it, what it cannot see
- [Manifesto](https://github.com/croviatrust/causari/blob/main/MANIFESTO.md)
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/croviatrust/causari/blob/main/ROADMAP.md)
- [GitHub Action](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/causari-survival-audit)
